raw_response:
I have farmed this land for forty years. I know what works here in Quzhou. Let me think through this year.

---

**Wheat — around 7 and a half mu, planted this coming October**

I buy improved seeds from the village input shop, same kind as my neighbor Lao Wang uses. He got 480 jin per mu last year. I plant about 11 kg seed per mu. At planting I work two bags of compound fertilizer — 50 kg per mu, the 15-15-15 kind — into the soil before I sow. Then in April when the wheat is at the knee, I spread 15 kg urea per mu as top dressing. I always water three times: once before the ground freezes in November, once at jointing in April, once when the grain is filling in May. I spray twice or three times — herbicide in winter, fungicide for the rust, and something for aphids in spring. I use rotary tillage after maize harvest to prepare the seedbed.

**Maize — same 7 and a half mu, planted right after wheat harvest in June**

I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, whatever the dealer has in stock. The ground is loose after wheat so I just do rotary. At planting I put about 50 kg compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow. When plants are knee-high I broadcast 20 kg urea per mu and water it in. Summers here get some rain, so I only irrigate once or twice — I watch carefully at silking, that is the critical time. I spray once for borer, once more if leaf disease shows up. Target is 600 kg per mu, same as last year.

**Cotton — the remaining 3 and a half mu**

Cotton is harder but the price can be good. I plough this land in spring. I use Bt hybrid seeds from the county seed company. Cotton needs more potash — my father-in-law taught me that — so I put extra potassium sulfate besides the compound fertilizer. I water it four times: before budding, at flowering, when bolls are setting, and once more in August if it is dry. Pest pressure on cotton is heavy here. I spray five times minimum — twice for aphids early, three times for bollworm through summer. Last year I got about 270 kg seed cotton per mu. I hope for 280 this year.

My biggest worry is fertilizer costs going up. Seven people in the house, and two kids' tuitions coming. I cannot cut corners on wheat and maize — those are our food and income. Cotton I will watch carefully before deciding whether to expand or cut back next year.
